sentences.text:
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the Award passed in M.V.C.No.842/2008, on the file of the FTC-2 & MMTC, Hassan, dated 09.03.2012, whereby the Tribunal had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.43,000/-.
2.
The claimant had filed a claim petition seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.6,00,000/-, on account of the injuries sustained by the claimant.

It is the case of the claimant that on 01.02.2008 at about 7 p.m after completion of land work he left towards his house, when he was going on the left side of the road, the rider of the Hero Honda bike came in a high speed and dashed against the claimant as a result of which he had sustained injury to the left foot also to NC: 2023:KHC:41250 the very same foot the third finger sustained grievous blood injury, apart from that 4th and 5th finger of the left foot was cut and he had spent huge amounts for treatment and was in hospital for a long time.

The Tribunal on the issue of liability had observed that at first, advocate for the 1st respondent itself has conducted the case of the claimant without bringing the same to the knowledge of the Court.
The Court came to know only on 31.12.2011 and it was submitted that his father was not feeling well and hence he could conduct the case.
Therefore, he had entrusted the file to 1st Respondent Advocate.
Accordingly, the advocate of the respondent No.1 himself was identifying the claimant, even at the time of filing an affidavit, he was identifying.
The Court below has come to the collusion that there is collusion between the parties and accordingly the Court below had fixed the liability on the owner of the vehicle.

3. When it comes to the compensation, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.20,000/-
under the head of pain and suffering.
Towards medical expenses granted an NC: 2023:KHC:41250 amount of Rs.10,000/-.
Towards unhappiness granted an amount of Rs.5,000/- and towards loss of income during laid up period an amount of Rs.8,000/-.
Altogether, the compensation of an amount of Rs.43,000/- was awarded by the Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that, for the injuries sustained by the claimant granting of an amount of Rs.20,000/- under the head of pain and suffering particularly, when there is an amputation of 4th and 5th toes, it was on the lower side.
It is submitted that as per the doctor, he had sustained 25% disability, no amounts were granted by the Court below under the head of loss of future income due to disability.

Even under the head of loss of amenities also no amount was Sri Shantharaju vs K Mohan Kumar on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8994600/
2 granted.

sentences.text:
It is submitted that when he was there in the hospital for two months, towards attendant,
nourishment and transport charges no amounts were granted.
It is submitted that the compensation that was granted by the Tribunal was on the lower side.

It is further submitted that the Court below without appreciating NC: 2023:KHC:41250 the evidence and fixing the liability basing on the fact that the 1st respondent advocate was also appearing on behalf of the claimant, had fixed the liability on the owner itself, which is not correct.
He submits that the claimant is a Mason & Agriculturist.
It is submitted that they are rustic Villagers and basing on that aspect, the Court cannot draw an inference and cannot fix the liability on the owner of the vehicle.
There should have been an independent finding basing on the evidence on record.
It is submitted that the Court below went wrong in exonerating the Insurance Company from the liability.
5. When this matter came up on 15.11.2023, there was no representation on behalf of the respondent Insurance Company.
Hence, the matter was adjourned to 16.10.2023 under the caption for Judgment.
Today also there is no representation on behalf of the Insurance Company.

As this is an accident of the year 2008, this Court is inclined to proceed with the matter basing on the merits of the case.
NC: 2023:KHC:41250
6. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellant, perused the entire material on record.
7. First coming to the aspect of liability the Court below ought not to have fixed the liability on the owner of the vehicle, basing on the fact that one advocate is representing both of them.
Though it was not proper, still the Court ought to have given a finding basing on the evidence available on record.
On this issue, this Court deems it appropriate to remand the matter to the Court below.
8. Then coming to the compensation, the claimant had sustained amputation of 2 toes.
Considering the said injuries and suffering, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.60,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
Towards treatment expenses the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.10,000/-, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.

Then coming to loss of income during the laid up period, considering the income at Rs.4,500/- per month, as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Ramachandrappa V/s Manager Royal Sundaram NC: 2023:KHC:41250 Alliance1.

9. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
